title: Internal HACCP audit: how to write a useful report
excerpt: Report structure, evidence-based nonconformities instead of opinions, and CAPA with a deadline and owner. A practical audit document accepted by any chain’s procurement team.

body.text: An internal audit is a regular part of a HACCP system. Your own team conducts it according to your own plan. The goal is to find problems before an inspector does. The resulting report is not a box to tick; it is a management tool.

items: Date and audit team (at least one auditor must be independent of the area being inspected).
Scope: what was checked (area, process, or shift).
Checklist and result for each item.
Nonconformities: level (critical, major, or observation), description, and evidence.
Signatures: auditor and manager of the inspected area.

body.text: State facts, not opinions. Instead of “it was dirty,” write: “Product residue was found on the shelf above the sink in the wash area; there are no cleaning records for this area from 10.03 to 12.03.”

body.title: CAPA is the heart of the system
body.text: Without a corrective action and a deadline, a nonconformity becomes a note “for the record.” Create CAPA as soon as the report is written and assign it to a specific person.

In WeSetup, an audit opens as a separate document: results, nonconformities, and CAPA stay together. A month later, it is easy to check whether every item is closed, and a nonconformity cannot be “lost” along the way.
